title: Taylor impact benchmark test activation
objective: Replace Taylor impact stubs with active tests for final length, mushroom radius, and equivalent plastic strain localization.

plan_assets.asset_description: Phase E8 active Taylor benchmark test acceptance criteria.

scope: Activate Taylor tests for final length, mushroom radius, and equivalent plastic strain localization.
Use deterministic smoke configuration for local test execution.
implementation_steps: Replace pytest.skip coverage in the Taylor impact test file.
Wire tests to the public Taylor impact runner.
Assert deterministic smoke outputs for geometry and state localization.
Mark full settings slow/nightly as required.
Run Taylor-specific tests and related runtime tests.
acceptance_criteria: Final length, mushroom radius, and equivalent plastic strain localization tests are active.
Tests are deterministic under smoke settings.
risks: Taylor impact can be expensive and sensitive to explicit time stepping; mitigate with deterministic smoke settings and nightly full settings.
completion_notes: Activated 3 P10-7 stubs in test_taylor_impact.py via Path A (frozen-reference regression). Markers (@nightly @regression @slow) + test names preserved exactly per AC.

Reference profile: TaylorImpactParameters.smoke(nz=20, n_steps=100, dt=1e-8, profile='regression'). Frozen values: final_length=0.02521 m, mushroom_diameter=0.011128 m, peak_peeq=2.84119. Tolerances 5%/5%/10% as named.
Added TestTaskP8_2Smoke class with 3 @integration smoke-tier tests (finiteness+schema, bit-for-bit determinism across 3 runs, parameter sensitivity on impact_velocity + wall_z).

Surfaced two P8-1 calibration issues (deliberately not fixed in P8-2 per brief): (1) shipped TaylorImpactParameters.nightly() overruns JC radial-return 50-iter budget on 6x6x20 mesh — worked around with reference profile derived from smoke; (2) PEEQ on long horizons (~16.6 at n_steps=200) is unphysical — JC hardening/thermal softening calibration needs a sanity pass. Both flagged in Phase 9 handoff.
